dno_dashboard.subtitle: 6 regional DSOs · ~5.3 M LV customers · 20 NUTS-3 megyék · 3,155 települések
dno_dashboard.intro: Hungary's distribution sector consolidated heavily during 2018-2024 around two parent groups: MVM Group (state-owned, ~60% market share) and E.ON Hungary (German, ~40% share). MVM acquired DÉMÁSZ + ELMŰ-ÉMÁSZ retail in 2018-2021, then pursued the E.ON Hungary portfolio from 2022 — the consolidation remains under MEKH + GVH competition review as of 2026-05-29, so the 6 DSO entities still operate as separately licensed Hungarian companies. MVM Elmű Hálózati (Budapest + Pest + Komárom-Esztergom, ~38%) is the highest-density block; E.ON Tiszántúli (Hajdú-Bihar + Szabolcs-Szatmár-Bereg + Békés-E + Jász-Nagykun-Szolnok, ~16%) covers the largest geographic area on the Great Plain. MVM Démász + Émász (Csongrád-Csanád/Bács-Kiskun south + BAZ/Heves/Nógrád north, ~22% combined) round out the state block; E.ON Észak-dunántúli + Dél-dunántúli (NW + SW Transdanubia, ~24%) complete the German block.

saidi.headline: Hungary's national SAIDI ~57 min/customer/year sits in the middle of the Visegrád+CEE-South range — better than Czechia, Poland and Slovakia, broadly comparable to Slovenia and Austria, behind the DACH and Nordic benchmarks. Urban Budapest metro achieves sub-30 min interruption durations on largely-underground sections, while the eastern rural E.ON Tiszántúli + MVM Émász networks average ~115 min restorations due to single-feeder Great Plain topology, NE/UA-border remoteness and 2001/2013 Tisza/Danube flood legacy.

notes.heading: Paks I + Paks II — Hungary's Single-Site Nuclear Concentration in Tolna megye
notes.sub_heading: 4-unit Paks I + Paks II Unit 5 First Concrete 5 Feb 2026
notes.body: All four Paks I VVER-440/V-213 units operate at a single site on the Danube's right bank in Tolna megye (HU233), ~100 km south of Budapest. Units 1-4 commissioned 1982-1987, ~500 MWe each post-uprate, combined ~1,916 MWe — generating ~45-50% of Hungarian electricity. License extensions through 2032-2037 are under OAH review with intent to extend to ~2052-2057. Paks II Units 5+6 (VVER-1200/V-491, ~1,200 MWe each) are co-located ~500 m from Paks I; Unit 5 First Concrete was poured 5 Feb 2026 by Rosatom + HU Foreign Minister Szijjártó — the first new-NPP first-concrete in any EU country since Hinkley Point C Unit 2 (Dec 2019), and the first Russian-built NPP in an EU member state. Target operation ~2031-2032 for Unit 5, ~2032-2033 for Unit 6 (Rosatom estimates). US OFAC sanctions on the project were lifted in Dec 2025. When fully operational, HU nuclear share could approach 70%+. The single-site concentration in HU233 elevates R3 + R6_seismic + R6c_flood at the megye level.

notes.heading: Mátra Lignite — Hungary's Last Coal Phase-Out (Repeatedly Postponed)
notes.sub_heading: End-2028 closure target + 500-650 MW CCGT replacement
notes.body: MVM Mátra (Visonta + Bükkábrány-fired units, ~880 MW lignite, Heves megye) is Hungary's last operating coal-fired generation. Lignite closure repeatedly postponed (2025 → 2027 → end-2028). The 500-650 MW CCGT replacement has been under construction since September 2025, targeted online 2028. MVM re-acquired Mátra from previous private consortium in 2020 for orderly phase-out. Contrast with SK Nováky (closed Dec 2023) and SI/CZ trajectories — Hungary lags the CEE coal-exit pattern. ISO 9223 C4 corrosion class assigned to the Visonta corridor pending closure. Mátra phase-out completion will mark Hungary's end of 70+ years of coal-fired electricity generation.

notes.heading: MAVIR Mukachevo–Sajószöged HU-UA Corridor — Active Emergency Sync
notes.sub_heading: 400 kV line · post-16 Mar 2022 Ukrenergo synchronization
notes.body: The 400 kV Mukachevo–Sajószöged line is Hungary's easternmost interconnect with Ukraine. Active since the 16 March 2022 emergency synchronization of Ukrenergo to Continental Europe; the legacy 750 kV Albertirsa–Vinnytsia line (Soviet CMEA backbone) has been decommissioned on the HU side post-1991. Unlike SK's Feb 2025 termination of the bilateral emergency-supply contract with Ukrenergo, Hungary has not (as of 2026-05-29) publicly terminated its arrangement — the PM Orbán government's TurkStream gas + Rosatom Paks II posture sets it apart from SK's and SI's stance on Russia-related energy flows. Commercial trade through the interconnect continues unaffected. Flag for V_socio / R7 modifier sensitivity in E.ON Tiszántúli's eastern territory.

deep_dive.label: Tolna megye — Paks I+II nuclear corridor
deep_dive.narrative: Tolna megye (HU233) is Hungary's single-site nuclear concentration zone. All four Paks I VVER-440/V-213 units operate at a single site on the Danube's right bank, ~100 km south of Budapest — Units 1-4 commissioned 1982-1987, ~500 MWe each post-uprate, combined ~1,916 MWe generating ~45-50% of Hungarian electricity. Paks II Units 5+6 (VVER-1200/V-491, ~1,200 MWe each) are co-located ~500 m from Paks I; Unit 5 First Concrete was poured 5 February 2026 by Rosatom — the first new-NPP first-concrete in any EU country since Hinkley Point C Unit 2 (Dec 2019), and the first Russian-built NPP in an EU member state. Target operation ~2031-2032 for Unit 5, ~2032-2033 for Unit 6. US OFAC sanctions on the project were lifted in Dec 2025. The Light-Rural R3 tier (1.06) reflects Tolna's predominantly agricultural character beyond the nuclear site, but the single-site concentration drives elevated R3 + R6_seismic + R6c_flood (Danube right-bank) modifier sensitivity at the corridor level. OAH safety oversight, ENTSO-E reserve obligations and MAVIR balancing cascade across the E.ON Dél-dunántúli DSO simultaneously in any Paks trip scenario. When Paks II Units 5+6 come online, HU nuclear share could approach 70%+ — among the world's highest.
